newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-MATCHES IN THE SPANISH FIRST DIVISION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MATCHES IN THE SPANISH FIRST DIVISION.

text.p: Matches scheduled for this weekend in the Spanish first division (league positions in parentheses, kick-off times GMT):
Deportivo, with six straight wins, have won two of their last three visits to San Sebastian, where Real Sociedad will be without striker Darko Kovacevic.

Valencia will be without star Argentine midfielder Ariel Ortega and several other key players for a crunch match against a Barcelona side also depleted by injury and international call-ups for World Cup matches.
Struggling Sevilla desperately need a result and are one of the teams least affected by international defections with only midfielder Robert Prosinecki absent because of a game with Croatia.
Athletic, who use only Basque players and are therefore unaffected by international call-ups, hope to capitalise in their game against a depleted and struggling Logrones side.
Extremadura look to striker Silvani and goalkeeper 'El Mono' Montoya in a bid to continue an extraordinary escape act which has seen them haul themselves up from bottom place in January.
Zaragoza have pulled themselves up five places in a month but tightness at the bottom of the table means they will be looking for a win to ease continuing relegation worries.

Manager Quique Hernandez rapped the knuckles of his players midweek amid growing defeatism in the Hercules camp created by an increasingly desperate situation. Racing still have hopes of a UEFA Cup place and will be looking for a result.

Espanyol will miss the speed of forward Miguel Angel Benitez who is playing for Paraguay. Betis will also be without key personnel in their bid to clock up a sixth successive league win for the first time since 1960.

Brazilian striker Guilherme could take up an unfamiliar position on the right wing as new Rayo coach Maximo Hernandez shuffles his pack in search of a winning combination. Oviedo striker Oli Alvarez is doubtful for the game with a groin strain.

The home side will be without Pablo Paz, Slavisa Jokanovic and Meho Kodro -- all on international duty. Real have lost 10 players for the same reason and because of an injury crisis for a fixture that traditionally gives them problems.
Daniel Prodan, Veljko Paunovic and Radek Bejbl will be out for Atletico, who saw their run of bad luck brought to an end last week in the last-gasp comeback at Rayo.
